judged_text: z.object strips unknown keys by default, so data parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema contains only access_token (plus the injected placeholder): in sync mode expiry_date/expires_in is never persisted, causing Office365/Zoom to re-refresh on every operation, and Salesforce (CalendarService.ts:~91) — which uses this schema whenever the feature flag is on even though its fetch goes directly to login.salesforce.com — has instance_url, signature and issued_at stripped from the stored credential, breaking the next jsforce.Connection.

adjudication.rationale: In `_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the code unconditionally parses token refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema. That schema is a `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`, so even if it succeeds it will not preserve extra fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, Salesforce `instance_url/signature/issued_at`) in `refreshTokenResponse.data`. This parsed `data` is then merged/persisted (e.g., Office365 `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.data) }`, Zoom uses the parsed result, Salesforce persists `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }`), so required fields can be lost in “sync mode,” breaking behavior. Additionally, the computed-key attempt (`[z.string().toString()]`) does not implement a true index signature, making the minimal schema unreliable for real responses.
